# Heisenbug & Goodman

> Runtime npm supply chain attack detection powered by eBPF. Know which dependency did it.

Heisenbug provides Goodman, an open-source, self-hosted security sensor built to track process, file, and network system calls inside production Node.js applications using Linux eBPF. Unlike static analyzers that scan files during build-time, Goodman tracks the exact runtime behavior of imported npm packages, maps anomalies to their version baselines, and alerts on behavior drift.

## Key Features

- **Runtime Attribution**: Attributes Linux kernel system calls directly to the originating npm package and version.
- **eBPF-powered**: Inspects system behavior at the kernel level with negligible CPU overhead.
- **Zero Configuration**: Learns baseline package behavior automatically and alerts on behavioral drifts.
- **Apache-2.0 License**: 100% open source, secure-by-default, and completely self-hosted inside your infrastructure.
- **Support & Deployments**: Helm charts for Kubernetes clusters, SQLite support for local dev, SSE stream APIs, and Prometheus integrations.

## Quick Start / Try It Locally

Clone the codebase and spin up the eBPF local docker demo (no root permissions required on host):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hi-heisenbug/goodman
cd goodman
make demo
```

To install on a Kubernetes cluster:

```bash
scripts/install-k8s.sh --cluster prod
scripts/enable-node-attribution.sh -n checkout --all
```
